newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon has chance to clinch Hughes deal - analyst. [CORRECTED 18:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Raytheon has chance to clinch Hughes deal - analyst. [CORRECTED 18:56 GMT]

text.p: Boeing Co's proposed acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp gives Raytheon Co "a window of opportunity" to buy Hughes Electronics Corp, Cowen & Co analyst Cai Von Rumohr said Monday. (Corrects day)
Hughes is a unit of General Motors Corp.
"It could put a little bit more pressure on Raytheon, but at the same time it takes two potential competitors out of the game for GMH," Von Rumohr said in a telephone interview.
"With the Boeing-McDonnell Douglas deal, Raytheon now has a short-term window" for completing a deal for Hughes, he said.
"It's not a long-term window. It will probably last until the (Boeing-McDonnell) deal is closed," he added.

"It's a dynamic situation," said Von Rumohr, who rates Raytheon neutral. "The folks at Hughes aren't stupid. They're not offering a price cut. And if they wait until the (Boeing-McDonnell) deal is done, there will certainly be an entity out there with more than enough cash capable of making the buy."
In early morning trading Hughes's stock rose 1-3/8 points. It later retreated to 56, up 7/8.

Executives at Raytheon, which reported $12 billion in sales for 1995, have long talked about reaching "a critical mass." In recent years the company has sought to diversify its businesses, expanding into commercial, engineering and construction and major appliances as a way of blunting cuts in U.S. defense spending.
